meta.title: Atlas of Life
meta.method: Ages, authorities, species and formations from the Paleobiology Database; descriptive data paraphrased from the cited literature and English Wikipedia; images from Wikimedia Commons and PhyloPic with their licences.

clades.name: Anhangueria
clades.sum: Large, toothed, often crested fish-eating pterosaurs of the Early to early Late Cretaceous (ornithocheirids, anhanguerids and kin).
diag: Jaw tips expanded into a tooth rosette
Rounded crests on the snout and/or lower jaw in many species
Very long wings
clades.notes: The most diverse and successful pterosaurs of the Early Cretaceous; include some of the largest toothed pterosaurs (Tropeognathus, ~8.3 m).

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Ornithocheiromorpha”. English Wikipedia, revision 1369303086.

clades.name: Anurognathidae
clades.sum: Small, short-faced, short-tailed ‘frog-jawed’ pterosaurs of the Jurassic and Early Cretaceous of Europe and Asia.
diag: Skull wider than long, with a very broad gape
Large eyes
Short tail
Peg-like or slender recurved teeth
clades.notes: Wingspans up to about 90 cm. Usually seen as aerial insect-catchers. Their position in the pterosaur tree is disputed.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Anurognathidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1384401713.

clades.name: Azhdarchidae
clades.sum: Long-necked, toothless ‘terrestrial stalkers’ of the Late Cretaceous, including the largest flying animals known.
diag: Very long, stiff neck vertebrae
Long toothless beak
Long legs and small feet suited to walking
clades.notes: Sizes from cat-sized to 10–12 m wingspans (Quetzalcoatlus, Hatzegopteryx). The last pterosaurs before the end-Cretaceous extinction.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Azhdarchidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383713244.
Witton, M. P.; Naish, D. (2008). A reappraisal of azhdarchid pterosaur functional morphology and paleoecology. PLOS ONE 3(5): e2271. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0002271

clades.name: Azhdarchoidea
clades.sum: Toothless pterodactyloids with relatively short arms and long legs, good walkers — from tapejarids to giant azhdarchids.
diag: Low arm-to-leg length ratio
Toothless jaws
Many with large head crests
clades.notes: Defined by Unwin (2003) as Quetzalcoatlus + Tapejara and all descendants. Several genera (Alanqa, Xericeps, Leptostomia, Keresdrakon, Inabtanin) are placed here as incertae sedis.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Azhdarchoidea”. English Wikipedia, revision 1369335323.
Unwin, D. M. (2003). On the phylogeny and evolutionary history of pterosaurs. Geological Society, London, Special Publications 217: 139–190.

clades.name: Boreopteridae
clades.sum: Long-snouted pterodactyloids with needle-like teeth, from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of China.
diag: Long, low snout
Long, sharp needle-like teeth, longest at the front
clades.notes: Placed near ornithocheirids by its describers but near Cycnorhamphus (Gallodactylidae) by Andres & Myers (2013). Placed here directly under Pterodactyloidea.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Boreopteridae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383158392.

clades.name: Chaoyangopteridae
clades.sum: Toothless, mostly Early Cretaceous azhdarchoids, probably ground foragers like azhdarchids.
diag: Very large nasoantorbital fenestra reaching back to the braincase
Toothless jaws
Long neck and legs
clades.notes: Defined by Lü & Unwin (2008). Sometimes treated as a subfamily (Chaoyangopterinae) of Tapejaridae.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Chaoyangopteridae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383158453.

clades.name: Ctenochasmatidae
clades.sum: Filter- and sieve-feeding pterosaurs with combs of long, thin teeth, from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous.
diag: Long snouts packed with many slender, often outward-pointing teeth
Teeth forming a filtering comb or basket
clades.notes: Andres (2021) recognised three subfamilies: Ctenochasmatinae, Gnathosaurinae and Moganopterinae.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Ctenochasmatidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383158638.
Andres, B. (2021). Phylogenetic systematics of Quetzalcoatlus Lawson 1975 (Pterodactyloidea: Azhdarchoidea). Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 41(sup1): 203–217.

clades.name: Ctenochasmatoidea
clades.sum: Early pterodactyloids — Pterodactylus, gallodactylids and ctenochasmatids — from the Late Jurassic to the late Early Cretaceous.
diag: Distinctive jaws and highly specialised teeth
Many species with numerous slender teeth
clades.notes: Kellner's broader Archaeopterodactyloidea also includes Germanodactylus; others prefer Ctenochasmatoidea/Euctenochasmatia for the lineage of Pterodactylus, gallodactylids and ctenochasmatids.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Archaeopterodactyloidea”. English Wikipedia, revision 1374260811.

clades.name: Darwinoptera (Wukongopteridae)
clades.sum: Jurassic transitional pterosaurs from China and England combining long tails with pterodactyloid-like heads and necks.
diag: Long tail and other ‘rhamphorhynchoid’ features
Long neck vertebrae
Nasoantorbital fenestra
clades.notes: Wukongopteridae was defined in 2010 (Wukongopterus + Kunpengopterus). Darwinoptera covers the same transitional lineage.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Wukongopteridae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383159371.

clades.name: Dimorphodontidae
clades.sum: Early, big-headed long-tailed pterosaurs of the Late Triassic to Early Jurassic, known from the UK and the south-western USA.
diag: Deep, lightly built skull with very large openings
Large external nostril, the largest skull opening
Fang-like front teeth followed by smaller teeth
clades.notes: Unwin's 2003 definition (Dimorphodon + Peteinosaurus) may be superfluous; Andres et al. (2014) used Dimorphodontia instead. Caelestiventus (2018) shows the group arose in the Triassic.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Dimorphodontidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383158668.

clades.name: Dsungaripteridae
clades.sum: Robust, inland pterosaurs of the Early Cretaceous with pincer-like jaw tips and crushing back teeth.
diag: Small eye socket placed high on the skull
High ridge across the snout
No teeth at the front of the jaws
Largest teeth at the back of the upper jaw
clades.notes: Commonly interpreted as eaters of hard-shelled prey. Their position (near azhdarchoids or elsewhere) is debated, so the family is placed here directly under Pterodactyloidea.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Dsungaripteridae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383158698.
Kellner, A. W. A. (2003). Pterosaur phylogeny and comments on the evolutionary history of the group. Geological Society, London, Special Publications 217: 105–137.

clades.name: Istiodactyliformes
clades.sum: Early Cretaceous pteranodontoids including the razor-toothed istiodactylids and the mimodactylids.
diag: Broad snouts
Teeth restricted to the front of the jaws; in istiodactylids triangular, compressed and interlocking
clades.notes: Istiodactylids are interpreted as scavengers. The contents of the group vary between analyses (Haopterus, Linlongopterus).

sources.text: Kellner, A. W. A. et al. (2019). First complete pterosaur from the Afro-Arabian continent: insight into pterodactyloid diversity. Scientific Reports 9: 17875. doi:10.1038/s41598-019-54042-z

clades.name: Monofenestrata
clades.sum: Pterosaurs in which the nostril and antorbital opening merged into a single large skull opening — pterodactyloids and their closest relatives.
diag: Nasoantorbital fenestra (single opening in front of the eye)
Elongated neck vertebrae
clades.notes: Named in 2010 after the discovery of Darwinopterus, which combines a pterodactyloid-type skull with a long tail. Several Jurassic forms (Douzhanopterus, Propterodactylus, Skiphosoura, Makrodactylus, Laueropterus) document the transition.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Monofenestrata”. English Wikipedia, revision 1353613677.

Lü, J.; Unwin, D. M.; Jin, X.; Liu, Y.; Ji, Q. (2010). Evidence for modular evolution in a long-tailed pterosaur with a pterodactyloid skull. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 277: 383–389. doi:10.1098/rspb.2009.1603

clades.name: Pteranodontia
clades.sum: Toothless, crested ocean soarers of the Late Cretaceous: Pteranodontidae and Nyctosauridae.
diag: Toothless jaws
Specialised head crests, larger in males
Very long, albatross-like wings
clades.notes: Restricted here to Pteranodontidae + Nyctosauridae, following Longrich, Martill & Andres (2018).

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Pteranodontia”. English Wikipedia, revision 1374690000.

Longrich, N. R.; Martill, D. M.; Andres, B. (2018). Late Maastrichtian pterosaurs from North Africa and mass extinction of Pterosauria at the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary. PLOS Biology 16(3): e2001663. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.2001663

clades.name: Pteranodontoidea
clades.sum: The most diverse Cretaceous pterosaurs: istiodactyliforms, anhanguerians, pteranodontids and nyctosaurids.
diag: Long, narrow wings with a warped deltopectoral crest on the humerus
Early forms toothed; later pteranodontians toothless
clades.notes: Defined by Kellner (2003) as Anhanguera + Pteranodon and all descendants; Ornithocheiroidea is sometimes treated as a synonym. Largely replaced by azhdarchids late in the Cretaceous.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Pteranodontoidea”. English Wikipedia, revision 1346803405.
Kellner, A. W. A. (2003). Pterosaur phylogeny and comments on the evolutionary history of the group. Geological Society, London, Special Publications 217: 105–137.

clades.name: Pterodactyloidea
clades.sum: Short-tailed pterosaurs, from the Middle–Late Jurassic to the end of the Cretaceous — the group that includes all the giants.
diag: Short tail
Long wing metacarpals
Long neck and large head
Hindlimbs free of the wing membrane; walked well on all fours
clades.notes: The most derived forms lost their teeth; by the Late Cretaceous all known pterodactyloids were toothless. Kryptodrakon (~161 Ma) is the earliest known member.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Pterodactyloidea”. English Wikipedia, revision 1371223005.
Andres, B.; Clark, J.; Xu, X. (2014). The earliest pterodactyloid and the origin of the group. Current Biology 24(9): 1011–1016. doi:10.1016/j.cub.2014.03.030

clades.name: Pterosauria
clades.sum: Pterosaurs: the first vertebrates to evolve powered flight, living from the Late Triassic to the end of the Cretaceous (about 228–66 Ma).
diag: Wing membrane of skin, muscle and other tissues stretched from a hugely elongated fourth finger to the ankles
Pteroid — a unique wrist bone supporting the membrane in front of the arm
Hair-like pycnofibres covering body and parts of the wings, in some cases branched like down feathers
Warm-blooded, with air sacs and flow-through breathing that hollowed out the bones
clades.notes: Traditionally split into long-tailed ‘rhamphorhynchoids’ (a paraphyletic grade) and short-tailed Pterodactyloidea, linked by the transitional Monofenestrata. Adult sizes range from about 25 cm to perhaps 10–11 m in wingspan.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Pterosaur”. English Wikipedia, revision 1385601836.
Andres, B.; Clark, J.; Xu, X. (2014). The earliest pterodactyloid and the origin of the group. Current Biology 24(9): 1011–1016. doi:10.1016/j.cub.2014.03.030

clades.name: Rhamphorhynchidae
clades.sum: Long-tailed Jurassic pterosaurs named after Rhamphorhynchus — the classic ‘rhamphorhynchoids’ with tail vanes.
diag: No more than 11 pairs of teeth in the snout
Deltopectoral crest narrow at its base and expanded at the tip
Bent phalanx on the fifth toe
Rhamphorhynchines: lightly built, pointed jaws with forward-pointing (procumbent) teeth
clades.notes: Traditionally divided into Rhamphorhynchinae and Scaphognathinae; not all analyses recover both groups.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Rhamphorhynchidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383159186.
Andres, B.; Myers, T. S. (2013). Lone Star pterosaurs. Earth and Environmental Science Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh 103: 383–398.

clades.name: Scaphognathidae
clades.sum: Robust, short-snouted long-tailed pterosaurs of the Jurassic, with few, widely spaced vertical teeth.
diag: Broad-tipped skull
Few, widely spaced, vertically oriented teeth
Robust skeleton and relatively short wings
clades.notes: Treated as a subfamily (Scaphognathinae) of Rhamphorhynchidae by many authors and as a separate family by others; both views place it among long-tailed breviquartossans.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Rhamphorhynchidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1383159186.

clades.name: Tapejaridae
clades.sum: Small to medium crested, toothless pterosaurs of the Cretaceous, probably of Asian origin — including the first known plant-eating pterosaurs.
diag: Bony crest arising from the snout, often supporting a larger soft-tissue crest
Very large nasoantorbital fenestra (at least half of skull length)
Small pear-shaped eye sockets
Downturned beak
clades.notes: Brain-case studies indicate excellent vision. Gut contents of Sinopterus show herbivory.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Tapejaridae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1385511302.

clades.name: Thalassodromidae
clades.sum: Large-crested azhdarchoids from the Albian Romualdo Formation of Brazil: Thalassodromeus, Tupuxuara and Kariridraco.
diag: Huge bony head crests
Toothless, blade-like jaws
clades.notes: Originally a subfamily of Tapejaridae; other analyses place it closer to azhdarchids and dsungaripterids. Placed here directly under Azhdarchoidea.

sources.text: Wikipedia contributors. “Thalassodromidae”. English Wikipedia, revision 1384648658.

genera.name: Alanqa
genera.isnote: Originally referred to Azhdarchidae; later analyses recovered it as a thalassodromid (Longrich et al. 2018) or as a basal azhdarchoid in its own clade, Alanqidae. Placed here at the most inclusive group all analyses agree on.
genera.sum: Large toothless azhdarchoid from the Cenomanian Kem Kem Group of Morocco, known almost entirely from straight, pointed jaw fragments.
genera.wsnote: About 4 m for the jaw specimens; an associated neck vertebra suggests individuals of about 6 m and 16–37 kg (Ibrahim et al. 2010).
genera.holotype: Jaw fragments from Aferdou N'Chaft near Begaa, SE Morocco.
genera.material: Five fragments of upper and lower jaws, possibly one neck vertebra; three further jaw specimens described in 2010.
genera.exceptional: Paired bony bumps where the jaws meet — possibly for display, soft-tissue anchoring or crushing hard-shelled food.
genera.biology: Lived on a freshwater delta. Inferred to have been a generalist predator taking crustaceans, molluscs, amphibians, small reptiles and possibly juvenile dinosaurs, like other azhdarchoids.
genera.author: Ibrahim et al. 2010

genera.name: Altmuehlopterus
genera.isnote: Separated from Germanodactylus as its own genus by Vidovic & Martill (2017); its relationships within Pterodactyloidea remain unresolved.
genera.sum: Late Jurassic pterodactyloid from the Solnhofen region of Bavaria with a large, beak-like snout (the species name refers to toucans). Formerly the informal nomen nudum “Daitingopterus”.
genera.holotype: BSP AS.I.745 — Mörnsheim near Daiting, Malm Zeta 3 (Tithonian), Bavaria.
genera.material: Partly articulated skeleton with skull, on plate and counterplate.
genera.biology: A small pterodactyloid of the Solnhofen archipelago lagoons; diet not specifically studied.
genera.author: Vidovic & Martill 2017

genera.name: Angustinaripterus
genera.sum: Middle Jurassic rhamphorhynchine from Sichuan, China, with a long, flat skull and a low crest.
genera.wsnote: Estimated by Wellnhofer (1991) from skull length.
genera.holotype: ZDM T8001 — Xiashaximiao (Lower Shaximiao) Formation, Dashanpu, Zigong, Sichuan.
genera.material: Single skull with lower jaws; left side badly damaged.
genera.biology: Long, curved, interlocking front teeth formed a ‘fish grab’, probably used to snatch fish from the water surface.
genera.author: He et al. 1983

genera.name: Anhanguera
genera.sum: Iconic crested ornithocheiriform from the Early Cretaceous of Brazil (Romualdo Formation), with rounded crests on the jaws and a spoon-shaped tooth rosette.
genera.wsnote: Wingspan of about 4.6 m for the largest specimens.
genera.holotype: Type species A. blittersdorffi, based on a complete skull from Romualdo Formation concretions, Ceará–Pernambuco, Brazil.
genera.material: Complete skulls; A. piscator is known from a nearly complete three-dimensional skeleton.
genera.exceptional: Uncrushed 3D preservation in carbonate concretions.
genera.biology: Fish-eater: long, angled conical teeth in a rosette for seizing slippery prey near the water surface. Jaw crests varied between individuals and may relate to age or sex.
genera.author: Campos and Kellner 1985

genera.name: Anurognathus
genera.sum: Tiny, short-faced ‘frog-jawed’ pterosaur from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestones of Bavaria.
genera.wsnote: Witton estimated 40 g for a specimen with a 35 cm wingspan.
genera.holotype: BSP 1922.I.42 — Solnhofen limestone near Eichstätt, Bavaria (found before 1922).
genera.material: Crushed, fairly complete skeleton, much of it only as an impression; a second, smaller subadult specimen is known.
genera.exceptional: The second specimen preserves impressions of the wing membrane and, under UV light, traces of limb muscles.
genera.biology: Insectivore with pin-like teeth and a very short, broad skull; probably caught insects on the wing. Possible bristles on the snout.
genera.author: Döderlein 1923

genera.name: Arambourgiania
genera.sum: Giant azhdarchid from Maastrichtian phosphates of Jordan, known chiefly from an enormous neck vertebra originally mistaken for a wing bone.
genera.wsnote: Early estimates of 11–13 m are now considered too high; recent estimates range from about 8–9 m (Paul 2022) to about 10 m (2024 study). 7 m has also been proposed.
genera.holotype: Holotype cervical vertebra (originally ~61 cm long) — phosphate mines near Russeifa, Jordan; found 1943.
genera.material: Incomplete neck vertebra; fragmentary material possibly from the same individual (metacarpal, femur, cervical fragments) described in 2018.
genera.biology: Like other azhdarchids, probably a terrestrial stalker feeding on small animals; known from a coastal marine setting.
genera.author: Nessov et al. 1987

genera.name: Arcticodactylus
genera.isnote: Formerly a species of Eudimorphodon; placed in Eudimorphodontidae by some, but the relationships of Triassic pterosaurs are unstable, so it is placed here directly under Pterosauria.
genera.sum: The smallest known pterosaur, from the Late Triassic of East Greenland.
genera.wsnote: Estimated 24 cm for the holotype individual.
genera.holotype: MGUH VP 3393 — Ørsted Dal Member, Fleming Fjord Formation (Norian–Rhaetian), East Greenland.
genera.material: Partial skeleton with skull.
genera.biology: Multi-cusped teeth (three to five points), fewer than in any other Triassic pterosaur; likely took small invertebrates.
genera.author: Kellner 2015

genera.name: Ardeadactylus
genera.isnote: Recovered in Ctenochasmatidae (Longrich et al. 2018) or Aurorazhdarchidae (Vidovic & Martill 2017); both fall within Ctenochasmatoidea.
genera.sum: Heron-like, long-necked pterodactyloid from the Late Jurassic of Bavaria, once a species of Pterodactylus.
genera.wsnote: Bennett (2013) estimated 1.45 m for the neotype; a referred specimen is about 10% larger.
genera.holotype: Original holotype lost in WWII; neotype JME-SOS 2428 (Jura Museum, Eichstätt), Solnhofen limestone.
genera.material: Two surviving specimens, including skull, neck and anterior body.
genera.biology: Interpreted as a long-legged wading piscivore; fewer and relatively larger teeth than Pterodactylus suggest larger fish prey.

genera.name: Aurorazhdarcho
genera.isnote: Bennett (2013) synonymised its type species A. primordius with “Pterodactylus” micronyx, and in 2025 argued that both are juveniles of Gnathosaurus subulatus. If accepted, Aurorazhdarcho would become a junior synonym of Gnathosaurus; kept separate here pending further study.
genera.sum: Small ctenochasmatoid from the early Tithonian of Bavaria; one specimen, the ‘Pester Exemplar’, may be the first pterosaur fossil ever documented.
genera.holotype: Type species A. primordius; the Pester Exemplar (holotype of A. micronyx) is a juvenile skeleton without skull, Solnhofen region.
genera.material: Several skeletons, mostly of juveniles.
genera.exceptional: The Pester Exemplar was first misidentified as a crustacean in the 18th century.
genera.biology: A small lagoon-dwelling pterodactyloid; ctenochasmatoids are generally associated with shorelines and small aquatic prey.
genera.author: Frey et al. 2011

genera.name: Austriadactylus
genera.isnote: Described as Pterosauria incertae sedis (Dalla Vecchia et al. 2002); some later analyses link it to Campylognathoididae, but no consensus exists.

genera.wsnote: Estimated at about 120 cm.

genera.name: Balaenognathus
genera.sum: Filter-feeding ctenochasmatid from the Late Jurassic of Bavaria, with more than 480 hooked, needle-like teeth.
genera.wsnote: Holotype wingspan 1.17 m.
genera.holotype: NKMB P2011-633 — Torleite Formation (late Kimmeridgian–Tithonian), Wattendorf, Bavaria.
genera.material: Nearly complete, articulated skeleton on 17 slab pieces.
genera.exceptional: Small patch of wing-membrane soft tissue preserved.
genera.biology: Spatula-shaped snout and comb-like dentition strongly suggest filter feeding in plankton-rich water, probably while wading or swimming rather than skimming in flight.

genera.name: Cacibupteryx
genera.sum: Rhamphorhynchine from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Jagua Formation of western Cuba.
genera.wsnote: Not estimated by the describers; said to be relatively large.
genera.holotype: IGO-V 208 — Jagua Formation, Pinar del Río, Cuba.
genera.material: Partial, uncrushed 3D skull (17 cm) and fragmentary left wing.
genera.exceptional: Three-dimensional skull.
genera.biology: Lived along the margins of the young Caribbean seaway; rhamphorhynchines were mainly fish-eaters.
genera.author: Gasparini et al. 2004

genera.name: Caelestiventus
genera.sum: Large Late Triassic dimorphodontid from a desert-dune setting in Utah — the only known desert-dwelling non-pterodactyloid.
genera.wsnote: At least 1.5 m, from an individual that was not fully grown.
genera.holotype: BYU 20707 — Saints & Sinners Quarry, Nugget Sandstone, NE Utah.
genera.material: Much of the skull (skull roof, face, complete mandible) and the last wing-finger bone.
genera.exceptional: Uncrushed braincase allowed the first endocranial reconstruction of a Triassic pterosaur.
genera.biology: Deep, narrow Dimorphodon-like skull; a possible throat pouch may have stored prey or served in display. Shows early pterosaurs were already ecologically diverse.
genera.author: Britt et al. 2018

genera.name: Caiuajara
genera.sum: Crested tapejarid from the Early Cretaceous ‘Pterosaur Graveyard’ of Paraná, Brazil, known from hundreds of bones of individuals of all ages.
genera.wsnote: Juveniles from 0.65 m; largest individuals about 2.35 m.
genera.holotype: CP.V 1449 — Goio-Erê Formation (Caiuá Group), Cruzeiro do Oeste, Paraná.
genera.material: Bonebed with hundreds of 3D bones: at least 47 individuals, including 14 partial skulls; holotype is a partial skeleton with skull.
genera.exceptional: Mass-death assemblage documenting growth: the crest grew larger and steeper with age.
genera.biology: The bonebed formed in a lake within a desert; mostly juveniles, possibly a nursery or crèche. Suggests gregarious behaviour. Toothless beak, like other tapejarines.
genera.author: Manzig et al. 2014

genera.name: Carniadactylus
genera.isnote: Separated from Eudimorphodon (as E. rosenfeldi) in 2009; placed in Campylognathoidea/Eudimorphodontidae by different authors. Relationships of Triassic pterosaurs remain unstable.
genera.sum: Small Late Triassic (Norian) pterosaur from northern Italy with complex multi-cusped teeth. The specimen once named “Bergamodactylus” is now included in it.
genera.wsnote: Holotype indicates about 70 cm; the paratype is a third smaller.
genera.holotype: MFSN 1797 — near Udine, Friuli, Italy (Dolomia di Forni).
genera.material: Partial skeleton with parts of skull and lower jaws, lacking the tail; paratype MPUM 6009 (Calcari di Zorzino, Lombardy) is an almost complete skeleton, largely as impression.
genera.biology: Multi-cusped teeth with little wear suggest a diet different from that of Eudimorphodon, probably softer prey such as insects.
genera.author: Dalla Vecchia 2009

genera.name: Cascocauda
genera.sum: Fluffy anurognathid from the Middle–Late Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Hebei, China, preserved with wing membranes and a dense coat of pycnofibres.
genera.wsnote: Holotype 434 mm; an immature individual.
genera.holotype: NJU-57003 — Mutoudeng locality (Daohugou bed), Tiaojishan Formation, Qinglong, Hebei.
genera.material: Nearly complete articulated skeleton on main and counter slab.
genera.exceptional: Extensive soft tissue: wing membranes and pycnofibres, some apparently branched like simple feathers (Yang et al. 2018).
genera.biology: Short, wide ‘frog-like’ jaws with long thin teeth and large eyes — an aerial insect-hunter. Its tail is relatively long for an anurognathid.
genera.author: Yang et al. 2022

genera.sum: Ctenochasmatid from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.holotype: IVPP V13756 — Yixian Formation, Liaoning.
genera.material: Single incomplete skull in dorsal view, left side damaged.
genera.biology: Teeth splaying outwards at the snout tip, like Ctenochasma; probably a filter feeder.

genera.name: Caupedactylus
genera.sum: Large crested tapejarine from the Romualdo Formation (Albian) of the Araripe Basin, Brazil.
genera.wsnote: Estimated by Kellner at 3.3 m — the largest known tapejarine.
genera.holotype: MN 4726-V — Romualdo Formation, Araripe Basin, NE Brazil.
genera.material: Partial skeleton with an almost complete skull (~46 cm), lower jaws and partial postcranium.
genera.exceptional: Acid-prepared, three-dimensional skull with well-preserved palate.
genera.biology: Toothless, downturned beak and a large, very thin head crest. Tapejarines are generally considered omnivores or plant-eaters.
genera.author: Kellner 2013

genera.name: Changchengopterus
genera.isnote: Placed in Rhamphorhynchidae (Lü 2009), tentatively in Wukongopteridae (Wang et al. 2010), and outside Monofenestrata (2017). Its position within long-tailed pterosaurs remains unresolved.
genera.sum: Small long-tailed pterosaur from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Hebei, China.
genera.wsnote: About 70 cm for the adult referred specimen (2011); 47.5 cm in earlier estimates.
genera.holotype: CYGB-0036 — Tiaojishan Formation (Callovian), Qinglong County, Hebei.
genera.material: Holotype: skeleton of a young juvenile, lacking the skull. Referred PMOL-AP00010: adult skeleton with lower jaws.
genera.biology: Part of the Yanliao Biota of forested lake shores; ecology not specifically studied.

genera.name: Chaoyangopterus
genera.isnote: Has also been placed in Tapejaridae (subfamily Chaoyangopterinae) by Pinheiro et al. (2011).
genera.sum: Toothless chaoyangopterid azhdarchoid from the Aptian Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: Estimated about 1.85 m.
genera.holotype: IVPP V13397 — Jiufotang Formation, Dapingfang, Chaoyang, Liaoning.
genera.material: Front of skull (~27 cm), lower jaws, neck vertebrae, shoulder and pelvic girdles, limbs.
genera.biology: Relatively short wings and long legs. Chaoyangopterids are thought to have resembled azhdarchids: crane-like terrestrial omnivores and opportunistic carnivores.

genera.name: Coloborhynchus
genera.isnote: Recovered in Anhangueridae or Ornithocheiridae depending on the analysis.
genera.sum: Large-crested anhanguerian from the Early Cretaceous of England, with front teeth set high on the blunt snout tip.
genera.wsnote: Based on the largest referred material, total skull length could reach 75 cm and wingspan about 7 m; species content varies between authors.
genera.holotype: BMNH 1822 — partial snout, Hastings Beds (Wealden Group), East Sussex, England.
genera.material: Partial snouts and jaw fragments; species assigned to the genus differ among authors.
genera.biology: Fish-eater with a crested, blunt snout and widely spaced fangs suited to seizing prey near the water surface.
genera.author: Owen 1874

genera.name: Cryodrakon
genera.sum: Giant azhdarchid from the late Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada — long referred to Quetzalcoatlus.
genera.wsnote: The holotype (immature) indicates at least 5 m; a large referred neck vertebra suggests about 10 m for mature individuals.
genera.holotype: TMP 1992.83 — Dinosaur Park Formation, Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta.
genera.material: Associated, disarticulated partial skeleton without skull: 4th cervical, rib, humerus, pteroid, 4th metacarpal, tibia, metatarsal; referred material from many individuals.
genera.exceptional: Holotype bones bear bite marks and an embedded tooth tip, probably from Saurornitholestes.
genera.biology: Lived inland on a coastal plain; like other azhdarchids, probably a terrestrial stalker of small animals.
genera.author: Hone et al. 2019

genera.name: Ctenochasma
genera.sum: ‘Comb-jaw’ ctenochasmatid from the Late Jurassic of Germany and France, with hundreds of long, thin teeth forming a basket.
genera.wsnote: Adult C. elegans reached a maximum of about 1.9 m.
genera.holotype: C. roemeri described from a single lower jaw (von Meyer 1851); three species recognised (C. roemeri, C. taqueti, C. elegans).
genera.material: Many specimens, mostly juveniles, from Solnhofen, the ‘Purbeck’ of NW Germany and eastern France.
genera.exceptional: The three species form a chronological series in which the filter apparatus became progressively refined (Bennett 2007).
genera.biology: Over 400 needle-like teeth in adults. Long seen as a filter feeder; the spoon-shaped tooth array may instead indicate spoonbill-like sweeping for small prey.
genera.author: Meyer 1851

genera.name: Cuspicephalus

genera.name: Cycnorhamphus
genera.isnote: Placed in Gallodactylidae, within Euctenochasmatia (Longrich et al. 2018).
genera.sum: ‘Swan-beaked’ gallodactylid from the Late Jurassic of Germany and France (= Gallodactylus) with bizarre, gaping jaws.
genera.holotype: GPIT specimen from Nusplingen, Württemberg (Kimmeridgian), described 1855.
genera.material: Several skeletons including the ‘Painten Pelican’ skull; one specimen destroyed in 1944.
genera.exceptional: Mineralised soft-tissue structures inside the jaw gap.
genera.biology: Peg-like teeth at the jaw tips and a gap behind them, possibly working like an openbill stork's to hold and crush molluscs and other hard invertebrates.
genera.author: Seeley 1870

genera.name: Darwinopterus
genera.sum: Classic transitional pterosaur from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China, combining a pterodactyloid-like head and neck with a long ‘rhamphorhynchoid’ tail.
genera.holotype: Type species D. modularis (Lü et al. 2010) — Tiaojishan Formation, Linglongta, Jianchang, Liaoning.
genera.material: 30–40 specimens, many complete skeletons; four species described, two of which have been argued to be junior synonyms of D. modularis (Zhou et al. 2021).
genera.exceptional: The egg-bearing specimen ‘Mrs T’ (ZMNH M8802), first described as Darwinopterus, was reassigned to Kunpengopterus antipollicatus in 2021.
genera.biology: Spike-like, widely spaced teeth; probably took small vertebrates and insects. Crests may relate to sex, though this is debated.
genera.author: Lü et al. 2010

genera.name: Dawndraco
genera.isnote: Many authors consider it a synonym of Geosternbergia/Pteranodon sternbergi; Kellner (2010) argued its stratigraphic position supports a separate genus.

genera.holotype: UALVP 24238 — lower Smoky Hill Chalk Member, Niobrara Formation, Kansas.
genera.material: Partial skeleton with almost complete skull and lower jaws.
genera.biology: Lived over the Western Interior Seaway; pteranodontids were ocean-going soarers that fed on fish.

genera.name: Dearc
genera.sum: Largest flying animal of its time: a big rhamphorhynchine from the Middle Jurassic of the Isle of Skye, Scotland.
genera.wsnote: Estimated 2.5–3 m; the holotype was still growing (proportional estimates range 1.9–3.8 m).
genera.holotype: NMS G.2021.6.1-4 — Lealt Shale Formation, Trotternish, Isle of Skye.
genera.material: Three-dimensional articulated skeleton missing the tail tip, most hindlimbs, parts of wings and beak tip.
genera.exceptional: Uncrushed 3D preservation including the braincase.
genera.biology: Long fangs at the snout tip and peg-like rear teeth suggest a fish-eater living around Jurassic lagoons.
genera.author: Jagielska et al. 2022

genera.sum: One of the smallest known pterosaurs, an anurognathid probably from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: About 40 cm.

genera.material: Near-complete, crushed skeleton of a subadult. A second species, D. mutoudengensis, is known from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation.
genera.biology: Short, broad skull and recurved teeth; a nimble aerial insectivore.

genera.name: Dimorphodon
genera.sum: Big-headed Early Jurassic pterosaur from the Blue Lias of England, named for its two kinds of teeth.
genera.wsnote: About 1.45 m; body length about 1 m.
genera.holotype: NHMUK PV R1034 — Blue Lias, Lyme Regis, Dorset (found 1828, Mary Anning).
genera.material: Partial disarticulated skeleton without skull; skulls known from NHMUK PV OR 41212 and R1035.
genera.biology: Deep, lightly built skull with fangs at the front and tiny lancet teeth behind. Dental microwear supports a predator of small vertebrates that may also have taken insects.

genera.wsnote: 74 cm (adult).
genera.holotype: STM 19-35 — Tiaojishan Formation, Linglongta, Liaoning (Shandong Tianyu Museum).
genera.material: Skeleton lacking the skull, on plate and counterplate.
genera.biology: Small, adult individual; ecology not specifically studied.

genera.name: Dsungaripterus
genera.sum: Robust, crested dsungaripterid from the Early Cretaceous of Xinjiang, China, with upturned pincer-like jaws.
genera.holotype: IVPP V-2776 — Lianmuqin Formation, Junggar Basin, Xinjiang.
genera.material: Partial skull and skeleton; further almost complete skulls from the Shengjinkou Formation.
genera.biology: Toothless pointed jaw tips to prise prey from crevices or mud, and knobbly rear teeth for crushing shellfish. Thick-walled bones suggest a largely terrestrial life.
genera.author: Young 1964

genera.name: Eopteranodon
genera.isnote: Has been placed in Chaoyangopteridae and as a basal tapejaromorph; most recent analyses place it in Tapejaridae.
genera.sum: Small crested, toothless tapejarid from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: About 1.1 m; a second specimen was larger.
genera.holotype: BPV-078 — Yixian Formation, Beipiao, Liaoning.
genera.material: Incomplete skeleton and skull (skull under 20 cm).
genera.biology: Toothless beak and large crest; tapejarids are thought to have included fruit and seeds in their diet.

genera.name: Eudimorphodon
genera.isnote: Usually placed in Eudimorphodontidae or Campylognathoididae; Triassic pterosaur relationships remain unresolved.
genera.sum: One of the oldest pterosaurs, from the Late Triassic (Norian) of Lombardy, Italy, with over 100 multi-cusped teeth.
genera.wsnote: About 1 m.
genera.holotype: MCSNB 2888 — Calcare di Zorzino, Cene, Bergamo (found 1973).
genera.material: Nearly complete skeleton; several further skeletons including juveniles.
genera.exceptional: Stomach contents with remains of the fish Parapholidophorus.
genera.biology: Fangs at the front and multi-cusped rear teeth that met when the jaws closed. A fish-eater that also took hard-shelled invertebrates; juveniles may have eaten insects.
genera.author: Zambelli 1973

genera.name: Europejara
genera.sum: The first European tapejarid, from the Barremian Las Hoyas Lagerstätte of Cuenca, Spain — at its description the oldest known toothless pterosaur.
genera.wsnote: About 2 m in the 2012 description; revised to 3–4 m in 2023 by some of the same authors.
genera.holotype: MCCM-LH 9413 — La Huérguina Formation, Las Hoyas, Cuenca, Spain.
genera.material: Rear of the skull with almost complete lower jaws, compressed on slab and counterslab.
genera.biology: Tapejarids are thought to have eaten fruit and seeds (perhaps also insects and small vertebrates); Europejara's age led its describers to suggest a role in seed dispersal of early flowering plants.
genera.author: Vullo et al. 2012

genera.name: Feilongus
genera.isnote: Originally placed in Gallodactylidae; Lü (2006) recovered it closer to Anhangueridae. Most later work keeps it among ctenochasmatoids, but its exact family is debated.
genera.sum: Large, double-crested ctenochasmatoid with a pronounced overbite, from the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: Estimated about 2.4 m by Wang and colleagues.
genera.holotype: IVPP V-12539 — Yixian Formation, Beipiao, Liaoning.
genera.material: Skull (39–40 cm) with articulated mandible and detached braincase, of a subadult; second skull DNMHM D3068 with four neck vertebrae.
genera.biology: 76 long, curved needle-like teeth confined to the jaw tips; probably caught small aquatic prey.
genera.author: Wang et al. 2005

genera.name: Ferrodraco
genera.sum: Crested anhanguerid from the Cenomanian–Turonian Winton Formation of Queensland — one of the most complete pterosaurs from Australia.
genera.wsnote: About 4 m and 10 kg.
genera.holotype: AODF 876 — Winton Formation, Queensland (found 2017).
genera.material: Front of skull and lower jaws, 40 loose teeth, five neck vertebrae, shoulder joint and parts of the left wing.
genera.exceptional: Largely 3D preservation in ironstone.
genera.biology: Anhanguerids are generally interpreted as fish-eaters; Ferrodraco had a high premaxillary crest and a toothed snout not expanded into a rosette.
genera.author: Pentland et al. 2019

genera.name: Forfexopterus
genera.sum: Scissor-jawed ctenochasmatid from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: Holotype (subadult) revised to 2.37 m; an adult wing specimen gives 1.78 m.

genera.biology: Long, low skull with slender outward-pointing teeth but no spatulate tip or crest; growth rates varied between individuals.

genera.isnote: Variously grouped with dsungaripteroids (Germanodactylidae) or with early ctenochasmatoids; Vidovic & Martill (2017) treat it as monotypic and moved ‘G. rhamphastinus’ to Altmuehlopterus.
genera.sum: Crested pterodactyloid from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestones of Bavaria — the first pterosaur known to have a soft-tissue crest.
genera.wsnote: 0.98 m for G. cristatus.
genera.holotype: BSP 1892.IV.1 (G. cristatus) — Solnhofen limestone, Eichstätt, Bavaria.
genera.material: Four specimens of G. cristatus, including two juveniles.
genera.exceptional: Head crest with a low bony ridge and a soft-tissue part more than doubling its height.
genera.biology: Sharply pointed jaw tip and robust teeth; a small predator of the Solnhofen lagoon.
genera.author: Young 1964

genera.name: Gladocephaloideus
genera.isnote: Placed in Gallodactylidae in 2012; a second skeleton (2016) shows it is a ctenochasmatid close to Pterofiltrus.
genera.sum: Sword-headed ctenochasmatid from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian) of western Liaoning, China.
genera.holotype: IG-CAGS-08-07 — Jingangshan Bed, Yixian Formation (early Aptian), western Liaoning.
genera.material: Almost complete skull (18 cm), lower jaws, front neck vertebrae and part of a hindlimb; juvenile skeleton JPM 2014–004 almost complete.
genera.exceptional: Short pycnofibres preserved at the back of the skull and neck.
genera.biology: About fifty sharp teeth restricted to the front quarter of the jaws; both known individuals are juveniles.
genera.author: Lü et al. 2012

genera.name: Gnathosaurus
genera.sum: Spoonbill-like ctenochasmatid from the Late Jurassic of Bavaria (and possibly the Purbeck of England); first mistaken for a crocodile.
genera.wsnote: About 1.7 m for the 1951 adult skull.
genera.holotype: Jaw fragment named Crocodilus multidens (1832), Solnhofen limestone; later G. subulatus.
genera.material: Skulls and jaws only (28 cm adult skull with up to 130 teeth); G. macrurus from a partial lower jaw and neck vertebrae.
genera.exceptional: Bennett (2025) argued that juvenile skeletons named Aurorazhdarcho micronyx belong to this species.
genera.biology: Needle-like teeth around a spoon-shaped tip: probably waded with open jaws and snapped them shut on small prey, like modern spoonbills.
genera.author: Meyer 1833

genera.name: Haliskia
genera.sum: ‘Sea phantom’: a large anhanguerian from the Albian Toolebuc Formation of Queensland — the most complete pterosaur from Australia.
genera.wsnote: Estimated 4.6 m from proportions of Arthurdactylus.
genera.holotype: KK F1426 — Toolebuc Formation, near Richmond, Queensland (found 2021).
genera.material: Partial skeleton (~22%): front of skull with partial crest, mandible, teeth, vertebrae, ribs, scapulocoracoid, limb bones.
genera.biology: Skeletally mature; lived over the Eromanga inland sea. Like other anhanguerians it was probably a fish-eater.

genera.name: Hamipterus
genera.isnote: Placed in its own family Hamipteridae within Pteranodontoidea/Anhangueria (Pêgas et al. 2019).
genera.sum: Colonial crested pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Hami, Xinjiang, China, known from bonebeds with eggs and embryos.
genera.wsnote: 1.5–3.5 m among the 2014 individuals.
genera.holotype: IVPP V18931.1 — Shengjinkou Formation (Tugulu Group), Hami, Xinjiang (skull, probably female).
genera.material: Remains of at least 40 animals in 3D, plus hundreds of eggs.
genera.exceptional: Uncrushed eggs and embryos; crest horn sheaths preserved; one of the most important pterosaur nesting sites.
genera.biology: Lived colonially by a lake. CT scans of embryos suggest hatchlings had well-developed legs but weak flight apparatus, and some parental care has been proposed.
genera.author: Wang et al. 2014

genera.name: Haopterus
genera.isnote: Grouped with Mimodactylus in Mimodactylidae within Istiodactyliformes (Kellner et al. 2019), but a 2024 redescription recovered it as a primitive ornithocheiriform.
genera.sum: Small crestless pteranodontoid from the Yixian Formation of Liaoning — the first Chinese pterosaur found with a skull.

genera.holotype: IVPP V11726 — Yixian Formation, Sihetun, Liaoning (found 1998).
genera.material: Front half of a subadult: skull (145 mm), lower jaws, girdle, sternum, wings, vertebrae, partial pelvis.
genera.biology: Twelve pairs of robust, recurved teeth; probably took fish and other small prey.

genera.name: Hatzegopteryx
genera.sum: Giant, heavy-skulled azhdarchid from the latest Cretaceous of Transylvania, Romania — the apex predator of the Haţeg island.
genera.wsnote: Largest remains suggest 10–12 m; other material from smaller individuals (4.5–6 m).
genera.holotype: FGGUB R 1083A — Densuş-Ciula Formation (Maastrichtian), Haţeg Basin, Romania.
genera.material: Two fragments of the back of the skull and the proximal left humerus; referred femur, scapulocoracoid and a large neck vertebra.
genera.exceptional: Very robust skull (estimated ~2.5 m long) and short, stout neck vertebra.
genera.biology: A terrestrially foraging azhdarchid; with no large theropods on Haţeg Island it was probably the apex predator, tackling dwarf titanosaurs and iguanodontians.
genera.author: Buffetaut et al. 2002

genera.name: Ikrandraco
genera.isnote: Recovered in Lonchodraconidae (sister to Lonchodraco).
genera.sum: Pterosaur with a blade-like keel under its lower jaw and none on the upper jaw, from the Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.holotype: IVPP V18199 — Jiufotang Formation, Liaoning.
genera.material: Partial skeleton with skull (28.7 cm), neck vertebrae, sternum, wings and foot; second skull IVPP 18406.
genera.exceptional: Unique crest combination with a hook-like rear process.
genera.biology: Small cylindrical teeth; the describers suggested the crest might be an adaptation for skim-feeding, though they did not regard skimming as likely.
genera.author: Wang et al. 2014

genera.name: Inabtanin
genera.isnote: Unresolved near the base of Azhdarchomorpha (Rosenbach et al. 2024); not formally assigned to a family.
genera.sum: Large toothless azhdarchoid from the latest Maastrichtian of Jordan — one of the most complete pterosaurs from Afro-Arabia.
genera.wsnote: Estimated 5.35 m (adult) — the only non-azhdarchid azhdarchoid above 5 m.
genera.holotype: YUPC-INAB-6-001–010 — Muwaqqar Formation, Russeifa, Jordan.
genera.material: Much of the jaws, four partial neck vertebrae, left scapulocoracoid and humerus, much of the right forelimb.
genera.exceptional: Three-dimensional bones studied by CT.
genera.biology: Lived alongside the giant azhdarchid Arambourgiania on the southern Tethys coast; diet unknown.
genera.author: Rosenbach et al. 2024

genera.name: Istiodactylus
genera.sum: Duck-billed-looking istiodactylid from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight, with razor-edged interlocking teeth.
genera.wsnote: 4.3–5 m; isolated bones may indicate up to 8 m. ‘I.’ sinensis from China was smaller (2.7 m).
genera.holotype: NHMUK R176 — Wealden/Vectis strata, Atherfield, Isle of Wight.
genera.material: Several 3D specimens: back of skull, skull, vertebrae, girdles and forelimbs.
genera.exceptional: One of the first pterosaurs known in three dimensions.
genera.biology: Interlocking triangular teeth acting like a ‘cookie cutter’ suggest a scavenger that cut morsels from carcasses (Witton; Martill).
genera.author: Howse et al. 2001

genera.name: Jeholopterus
genera.sum: Fuzzy anurognathid from the Daohugou beds of Inner Mongolia, China, preserved with a halo of pycnofibres.
genera.wsnote: About 90 cm.
genera.holotype: IVPP V12705 — Daohugou beds (Tiaojishan Formation), Ningcheng, Inner Mongolia.
genera.material: Nearly complete crushed skeleton on slab and counterslab.
genera.exceptional: Carbonised skin fibres, pycnofibres and wing tissue; a possible Cretaceous specimen from North Korea.
genera.biology: Very broad mouth with peg-like and recurved teeth; anurognathids are considered insectivores, though Jeholopterus, the largest, may also have eaten fish.
genera.author: Wang et al. 2002

genera.name: Jianchangnathus
genera.sum: Scaphognathus-like long-tailed pterosaur from the Middle–Late Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China.

genera.isnote: Assigned by its describers to Scaphognathinae within Rhamphorhynchidae.

genera.name: Keresdrakon
genera.isnote: Recovered as the earliest-diverging tapejaromorph (Kellner et al. 2019) or as sister to Alanqa at the base of Azhdarchoidea (Pêgas et al. 2022).
genera.sum: Toothless azhdarchoid from the Early Cretaceous ‘Pterosaur Graveyard’ of Paraná, Brazil, found with Caiuajara and the theropod Vespersaurus.
genera.holotype: CP.V 2069 — Goio-Erê Formation (bonebed C), Cruzeiro do Oeste, Paraná.
genera.material: Disarticulated 3D partial skeleton of a subadult: snout, quadrate, lower jaws, vertebrae, sternum, girdles and limb bones.
genera.biology: Found in direct association with the tapejarid Caiuajara and the noasaurid theropod Vespersaurus, showing the three lived together around a desert lake.

genera.name: Kunpengopterus
genera.sum: Wukongopterid from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China; K. antipollicatus (‘monkeydactyl’) had an opposable thumb.
genera.holotype: IVPP V16047 (K. sinensis) — Tiaojishan Formation, Linglongta, Jianchang, Liaoning.
genera.material: Almost complete skeletons with skulls; several specimens.
genera.exceptional: Possibly regurgitated fish with the holotype; ‘Mrs T’ (ZMNH M8802), now K. antipollicatus, preserves an egg; the first known opposed thumb in a pterosaur.
genera.biology: The opposable thumb, rare in non-mammals, suggests a grasping ability. Low bony crest behind the eyes, extended by cartilage and perhaps a skin flap.
genera.author: Wang et al. 2010

genera.name: Leptostomia
genera.isnote: Described as ?Azhdarchoidea; known material too limited for a confident family assignment.
genera.sum: Small azhdarchoid from the Kem Kem Group of Morocco with an extraordinarily thin, long beak.
genera.wsnote: Skull length estimated 6–20 cm — much smaller than most contemporaries.
genera.holotype: FSAC-KK 5075 — Kem Kem Group, near Hassi El Begaa, Morocco.
genera.material: Two isolated beak fragments (upper beak and lower beak).
genera.biology: Slender, slightly upcurved toothless beak with many sensory foramina, suggesting a probe-feeder that searched sediment for invertebrates, like curlews, woodcocks and kiwis (Smith et al. 2020).
genera.author: Smith et al. 2020

genera.name: Ludodactylus
genera.sum: Toothed pterosaur with a Pteranodon-like head crest, from the Crato Formation of Brazil — named after the inaccurate toy pterosaurs it resembles.
genera.wsnote: Skull over 66 cm long.
genera.holotype: SMNK PAL 3828 — Nova Olinda Member, Crato Formation, Ceará.
genera.material: Skull missing part of the crest (removed before illegal sale).
genera.exceptional: A plant leaf stuck between the lower jaws, possibly contributing to its death.
genera.biology: No snout crest but a crest at the back of the skull; a fish-eating anhanguerian.
genera.author: Frey et al. 2003

genera.name: Noripterus
genera.sum: Lighter-built dsungaripterid from the Early Cretaceous of Xinjiang, China, living alongside Dsungaripterus.
genera.wsnote: Maximum about 4 m if ‘Phobetor’ material from Mongolia is included.
genera.holotype: IVPP V.4062 — Lianmuqin Formation, Junggar Basin, Xinjiang.
genera.material: Front of skull and lower jaws, vertebrae, partial limbs and pelvis; further material including an almost complete skull (GIN 100/31, ‘Phobetor’).
genera.biology: Toothless beak tip for probing and picking up prey, and teeth further back for cracking shells; its slenderer teeth suggest a different niche from Dsungaripterus around inland lakes.

genera.sum: Transitional monofenestratan — formerly the ‘Painten pro-pterodactyloid’ — from the Late Jurassic Painten Formation of Bavaria.
genera.wsnote: About 55 cm (juvenile or subadult).
genera.holotype: DMA-JP-2011/006 — Painten Formation, Rygol quarry, Painten, Bavaria.
genera.material: Complete articulated skeleton.
genera.exceptional: Soft tissues preserved.
genera.biology: Skull proportions most similar to Pterodactylus; mosaic of primitive and pterodactyloid traits.
genera.author: Spindler 2024

genera.name: Pteranodon
genera.sum: Iconic crested, toothless pterosaur of the Western Interior Seaway, known from about 1,200 specimens.
genera.wsnote: Females about 3.8 m; males 5.6–7.6 m.
genera.holotype: YPM 1117 skull (P. longiceps) — Smoky Hill Chalk, Niobrara Formation, Kansas.
genera.material: About 1,200 specimens, many with nearly complete skulls and articulated skeletons.
genera.exceptional: Fish bones in the stomach region and a fish bolus; clear sexual dimorphism in crest and pelvis.
genera.biology: Albatross-like soaring wings; fed on fish, probably dipping or plunge-diving from the surface. Males with huge crests may have competed for harems at offshore rookeries.
genera.author: Marsh 1876

genera.name: Pterodactylus
genera.isnote: Recovered as the most basal member of Euctenochasmatia.
genera.sum: The first pterosaur ever named, from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria.
genera.wsnote: About 1.04 m, based on the only known adult.
genera.holotype: BSP AS.I.739 — Solnhofen limestone, Eichstätt, Bavaria (described 1784).
genera.material: Over 30 specimens, mostly juveniles, many complete.
genera.exceptional: Some specimens show a low bony crest and an occipital lappet.
genera.biology: A generalist carnivore; tooth wear suggests it mainly ate invertebrates.
genera.author: Cuvier 1809

genera.name: Pterodaustro
genera.sum: Flamingo-like filter feeder from the Early Cretaceous of San Luis, Argentina, with about a thousand bristle-like teeth.
genera.wsnote: Maximum adult about 3 m and 9.2 kg.
genera.holotype: PVL 2571 (femur) — Lagarcito Formation, San Luis, Argentina.
genera.material: Over 750 specimens from all growth stages, from egg to adult.
genera.exceptional: Embryo in an egg (2004) and 3D eggs (2014); possible medullary bone.
genera.biology: Strongly upcurved jaws with a comb of long bristle-teeth for straining crustaceans and plankton. Bakker suggested a flamingo-like pink colour from its diet.
genera.author: Bonaparte 1970

genera.name: Pterorhynchus
genera.sum: Long-tailed pterosaur with a large keratin head crest, from the Daohugou beds of Inner Mongolia, China.
genera.wsnote: About 85 cm.
genera.holotype: CAGS02-IG-gausa-2/M 608 — Daohugou beds, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia.
genera.material: Articulated, nearly complete skeleton.
genera.exceptional: Wing membrane, pycnofibres, a long tail vane, and a crest with a bony base and large keratin extension.
genera.biology: Skull 11.8 cm; its describers suggested the crest had an aerodynamic function.
genera.author: Czerkas and Ji 2002

genera.name: Quetzalcoatlus
genera.isnote: A 2025 analysis suggested Q. lawsoni may not be closely related to Q. northropi.
genera.sum: One of the largest flying animals ever: a giant azhdarchid from the latest Cretaceous of Texas.
genera.wsnote: Q. northropi about 10–11 m; Q. lawsoni about 4.5–5 m.
genera.holotype: TxVP 41450-3 (Q. northropi) — Javelina Formation, Big Bend, Texas (found 1971).
genera.material: Holotype a partial left wing; Q. lawsoni known from many individuals with skull material.
genera.biology: Usually reconstructed as a terrestrial stalker hunting small animals on foot, like storks or ground hornbills; Q. lawsoni lived around alkaline lakes and may have eaten aquatic invertebrates.
genera.author: Lawson 1975

genera.name: Raeticodactylus
genera.isnote: Grouped with Caviramus in Raeticodactylidae (Andres et al. 2014); its broader relationships are unstable.
genera.sum: Crested Late Triassic pterosaur from the Kössen Formation of Grisons, Switzerland.
genera.wsnote: About 135 cm.
genera.holotype: BNM 14524 — Alplihorn Member, Kössen Formation, Grisons (found 2005).
genera.material: Disarticulated partial skeleton with an almost complete skull.
genera.exceptional: Tall thin crest on the upper jaw and a keel under the lower jaw.
genera.biology: Fang-like front teeth and multi-cusped cheek teeth; may have been a fish-eater (the skim-feeding idea is now rejected).
genera.author: Stecher 2008

genera.name: Rhamphorhynchus
genera.sum: Classic long-tailed pterosaur with a diamond-shaped tail vane, from the Late Jurassic of Germany and beyond.
genera.wsnote: 29 cm to about 1.8 m; one possible specimen may exceed 3 m.
genera.holotype: TM 6924 (R. longicaudus; Teylers Museum) — Solnhofen limestone, Bavaria.
genera.material: Many specimens, often complete, from very small juveniles (29 cm) to adults.
genera.exceptional: Fish and cephalopods in the stomach and coprolites; slab WDC CSG 255 shows one caught by the fish Aspidorhynchus while swallowing a fish.
genera.biology: Forward-angled needle teeth for catching fish. Scleral-ring comparisons suggest it may have been nocturnal, unlike the contemporary Scaphognathus and Pterodactylus.
genera.author: Meyer 1847

genera.name: Scaphognathus
genera.sum: Short, blunt-snouted long-tailed pterosaur from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestones of Bavaria.
genera.wsnote: Adult about 0.9 m; juvenile about 0.5 m.
genera.holotype: Holotype (described 1831 as Pterodactylus crassirostris) — Solnhofen limestone, Eichstätt.
genera.material: Three specimens.
genera.biology: Vertical teeth and a blunt, boat-shaped lower jaw. Scleral rings suggest it may have been diurnal.
genera.author: Wagner 1861

genera.name: Sericipterus
genera.sum: Large, triple-crested rhamphorhynchine from the Late Jurassic Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang, China.
genera.wsnote: At least 1.73 m.
genera.holotype: IVPP V14725 — Shishugou Formation (early Oxfordian), Junggar Basin, Xinjiang.
genera.material: Partly crushed, disarticulated bones, largely 3D.
genera.exceptional: First parietal crest reported in a non-pterodactyloid.
genera.biology: Recurved, keeled teeth with cutting edges; large rhamphorhynchines like it are thought to have lived inland as predators of small tetrapods.
genera.author: Andres et al. 2010

genera.name: Shenzhoupterus
genera.isnote: Also recovered within Tapejaridae (Chaoyangopterinae) by Pinheiro et al. (2011).
genera.sum: Toothless chaoyangopterid with a crest arching over the eyes, from the Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
genera.wsnote: About 1.4 m.
genera.holotype: HGM 41HIII-305A (Henan Geological Museum) — Jiufotang Formation, Liaoning.
genera.material: Articulated skull and skeleton of one individual.
genera.biology: A small toothless azhdarchoid, probably a ground forager.

genera.name: Sinomacrops
genera.sum: Anurognathid from the Daohugou beds of Hebei, China — one of the best-known members of its family.
genera.holotype: JPM-2012-001 — Daohugou beds (Tiaojishan Formation), Mutoudeng, Qinglong, Hebei.
genera.material: Crushed, almost complete skeleton (many bones as impressions).
genera.exceptional: Soft tissue suggests the arm membrane extended to the lower leg.
genera.biology: Very long lower legs (twice the femur); an insect-catching anurognathid.
genera.author: Wei et al. 2021

genera.name: Sinopterus
genera.sum: Toothless, crested tapejarid from the Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China — the first pterosaur with direct evidence of plant-eating.
genera.wsnote: Holotype about 1.2 m; maximum adult about 1.9 m (2.87 kg).
genera.holotype: IVPP V13363 (S. dongi) — Jiufotang Formation, Chaoyang, Liaoning.
genera.material: Numerous specimens at various growth stages; several former species now synonymised with S. dongi.
genera.exceptional: Gut contents with gastroliths and plant phytoliths (grasses, gymnosperms or ferns).
genera.biology: Herbivore with a gizzard similar to that of the bird Jeholornis; growth series documents crest development.
genera.author: Wang and Zhou 2002

genera.name: Skiphosoura
genera.isnote: Recovered as a non-pterodactyloid member of Pterodactyliformes (Hone et al. 2024).
genera.sum: ‘Sword tail’: a transitional monofenestratan from the Late Jurassic Mörnsheim Formation of Bavaria, with a short, stiff tail.
genera.wsnote: 1.75 m; may not have been fully grown.
genera.holotype: LF 4157 (Lauer Foundation) — Mörnsheim Formation, Schaudiberg Quarry, Bavaria.
genera.material: Nearly complete, disarticulated skeleton with partial skull, many bones in 3D.
genera.biology: Body plan intermediate between long-tailed pterosaurs and pterodactyloids.
genera.author: Hone et al. 2024

genera.name: Sordes
genera.isnote: Usually assigned to Rhamphorhynchidae (Scaphognathinae).
genera.sum: ‘Hairy devil’ from the Late Jurassic Karabastau Formation of Kazakhstan — the first clear proof that pterosaurs were furry.
genera.wsnote: About 63 cm.
genera.holotype: PIN 2585/3 — Karabastau Formation, Kazakhstan.
genera.material: Several relatively complete skeletons (at least eight by 2003).
genera.exceptional: Pycnofibres and wing membranes, including a membrane between the legs.
genera.biology: Large front teeth for catching prey and smaller rear teeth for crushing — perhaps hard-shelled invertebrates or amphibians.
genera.author: Sharov 1971

genera.name: Tapejara
genera.sum: Small tapejarid with a semicircular snout crest, from the Santana Group of Brazil.
genera.holotype: MN 6595-V — Romualdo Formation, Araripe Basin (survived the 2018 Museu Nacional fire, condition unknown).
genera.material: Partial skulls (AMNH 24440 with mandible and a neck vertebra).
genera.biology: Toothless downturned beak; bite-force studies suggest a herbivorous diet of fruit, seeds and tougher plant matter.

genera.name: Thalassodromeus
genera.isnote: Thalassodromids are treated as a subfamily of Tapejaridae by some authors and as close to azhdarchids by others.
genera.sum: ‘Sea runner’: the largest thalassodromid, with a huge bony head crest, from the Romualdo Formation of Brazil.
genera.wsnote: 4.2–4.5 m, based on related pterosaurs.
genera.holotype: DGM 1476-R — Romualdo Formation, Santana do Cariri, Ceará (found 1983).
genera.material: Almost complete 3D skull.
genera.exceptional: Huge, blood-vessel-rich crest.
genera.biology: Originally thought to skim the water like a skimmer bird; experiments rejected this. Its strong jaws suggest it may have killed fairly large prey on the ground.
genera.author: Kellner and Campos 2002

genera.name: Torukjara
genera.sum: Tapejarine from the ‘Pterosaur Graveyard’ of Paraná, Brazil, living alongside its close relative Caiuajara.
genera.holotype: CP.V 8175 — Caiuá Group (Goio-Erê/Rio Paraná Formation), Cruzeiro do Oeste, Paraná (found 2014).
genera.material: Partial skeleton with a well-preserved skull; several specimens.
genera.biology: Toothless crested tapejarine of a desert-lake setting.
genera.author: Pêgas 2024

genera.name: Tropeognathus
genera.isnote: Recovered in Anhangueridae or Ornithocheiridae depending on the analysis.
genera.sum: Largest pterosaur of the Southern Hemisphere apart from azhdarchids: a keel-jawed giant from the Romualdo Formation of Brazil.
genera.wsnote: About 8.26 m for specimen MN 6594-V; maximum estimate 8.7 m.
genera.holotype: BSP 1987 I 46 — Romualdo Formation, Santana Group, Ceará.
genera.material: Skull with lower jaws; large skeleton MN 6594-V (Tropeognathus cf. mesembrinus) with most of the body.
genera.biology: Rounded keels on both jaw tips; like other anhanguerians, probably a fish-eater.
genera.author: Wellnhofer 1987

genera.name: Tupandactylus
genera.sum: Tapejarid with an enormous sail-like head crest of bone and keratin, from the Crato Formation of Brazil.
genera.wsnote: T. imperator 3–4 m; T. navigans about 2.7 m.
genera.holotype: MCT 1622-R — Crato Formation, Ceará.
genera.material: Skulls and a very complete T. navigans skeleton (2021).
genera.exceptional: Soft-tissue crest and keratin beak preserved; filament-like integument.
genera.biology: Crest about one third of the wingspan in length; the two species may be sexes of one dimorphic species. Toothless beak.
genera.author: Kellner and Campos 2007

genera.name: Tupuxuara
genera.sum: Large thalassodromid with a big bony crest, from the Romualdo Formation of Brazil.
genera.wsnote: About 4.7 m and 25 kg (Paul 2022).
genera.holotype: MN 6591-V (T. longicristatus) — Romualdo Formation, Araripe Basin.
genera.material: Snout and partial wing bones (holotype); several skulls of T. leonardii.
genera.biology: Long wings relative to body mass; the crest was mostly bone.
genera.author: Kellner and Campos 1988

genera.name: Vesperopterylus
genera.sum: Youngest known anurognathid, from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China, with a reversed first toe.
genera.holotype: Holotype — Jiufotang Formation, Liaoning (Lü et al. 2017).
genera.material: Articulated skeleton.
genera.biology: A reversed first toe and sharp curved claws suggest it climbed or clung to tree branches.
genera.author: Lu et al. 2017

genera.name: Wellnhopterus
genera.sum: Short-faced azhdarchid from the Maastrichtian Javelina Formation of Big Bend, Texas.
genera.wsnote: About 3 m (Andres & Langston 2021).
genera.holotype: TxVP 42489-2 — Javelina Formation, Big Bend National Park, Texas.
genera.material: Upper and lower jaws, several neck vertebrae and a fragmentary long bone.
genera.biology: Unusually blunt, short jaws for an azhdarchid.
genera.author: Andres and Langston 2021

genera.name: Wukongopterus
genera.sum: Wukongopterid from the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China, with both a long neck and a long tail.
genera.wsnote: About 73 cm.
genera.holotype: IVPP V15113 — Tiaojishan Formation, Liaoning.
genera.material: Nearly complete compressed skeleton lacking the back and middle of the skull.
genera.biology: May have had a membrane between the hind legs (uropatagium).
genera.author: Wang et al. 2009

genera.name: Xericeps
genera.isnote: Consistently recovered with Alanqa and Leptostomia in Alanqidae, whose position within Azhdarchoidea is debated.
genera.sum: Toothless pterosaur with a forceps-like, upturned beak from the Kem Kem beds of Morocco.
genera.wsnote: Probably near the lower end of 3–8 m.
genera.holotype: FSAC-KK-10700 — Kem Kem Group, Aferdou N'Chaft, near Hassi el Begaa, Morocco.
genera.material: Fragmented front of the lower jaw.
genera.biology: Upturned forceps-like beak; alanqids are thought to have fed on molluscs or by probing.
genera.author: Martill et al. 2018

genera.name: Yixianopterus
genera.isnote: Assigned to Lonchodectidae (Lü et al. 2006) and later recovered as a basal istiodactyliform (Jiang et al. 2020).
genera.sum: Pterodactyloid from the uppermost Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China; much of the original skull was fabricated by dealers.
genera.holotype: JZMP-V-12 (Benxi Geological Museum) — Jingangshan bed, Yixian Formation, Liaoning.
genera.material: Right forelimb, a foot and teeth (skull largely fabricated).
genera.biology: Triangular, laterally compressed teeth.

genera.name: Zhejiangopterus
genera.sum: The most completely known azhdarchid, from the Campanian Tangshang Formation of Zhejiang, China.
genera.wsnote: About 3.5 m (first estimated 5 m); about 7.9 kg (Witton).
genera.holotype: ZMNH M1330 — Tangshang Formation, Linhai, Zhejiang.
genera.material: Several skeletons, including an almost complete one, and a complete skull.
genera.biology: Long, sharply pointed toothless beak; a ground-foraging azhdarchid.
genera.author: Cai and Wei 1994
